the cardiac-related power in the autospectrum of MSNA of humans is not simply a reflection of its linear relationship to heart rate, but is instead the manifestation of a nonlinear process.
the cardiac-related oscillation in muscle sympathetic nerve discharge of humans is a manifestation of a central oscillator that is entrained by the pulse-synchronous baroceptor discharge.

understanding the basis for the cardiac-related oscillation in MSNA of humans, which is the basis for the baroreflex-mediated oscillation in MSAA.
the mechanisms that underlie the rhythmic nature of sympathetic activity.
the control of muscle sympathetic nerve activity in humans.

there are multiple, complex, and nonlinear mechanisms that underlie the generation of cardiac-related bursts in MSNA of humans.

the cardiac-related MSNA rhythm in humans is complex, and its basis remains to be fully elucidated.

the cardiac-related MSNA rhythm reflects entrainment of an intrinsic, nonlinear central oscillator by baroreceptor nerve traffic.

the cardiac-related MSNA rhythm reflects the interaction of two nonlinear oscillators, the baroreceptor nerve and the MSNA generator, which are coupled to each other through a nonlinear, phase-dependent mechanism.

the cardiac-related oscillation of muscle sympathetic nerve activity is not due to entrainment of the central oscillator by pulse synchronous baroreceptor nerve discharge.
